svg.text: largest swing -- can roll or sideswipe

text.font-family: Liberation Sans, DejaVu Sans, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif
text.tspan: Why it matters: the last trailer can swing far enough to roll over, hit another vehicle, or leave the lane even when the tractor did not.
Triples and long doubles amplify this more than a single trailer. The rear is also harder to see.
Prevent it: steer smoothly, do not make sudden lane changes, and slow down early. Do not use the trailer hand valve to straighten a jackknife -- that can make a skid worse.
Backing doubles/triples is generally not recommended except for a short, straight, carefully watched move.
